papers_read.title_as_printed: Effects of aerobic exercise on global cognitive function and sleep in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: A systematic review and meta-analysis
Effects of exergaming in older individuals with mild cognitive impairment and dementia: A systematic review and meta-analysis

what_each_reports.P-698: Ahn & Kim, Geriatric Nursing 2023;51:9-16 (PROSPERO CRD42022343916). 11 RCTs of single-modality aerobic exercise versus health education, stretching or usual activity in adults >=60 meeting MCI criteria (Petersen 1999, DSM-5); 715 analysed. Global cognition (MMSE, MoCA or NCSE; Hedges' g, random effects): SMD 0.76, 95% CI 0.37-1.14 in the abstract but 0.37-0.91 in the Results (the sensitivity section cites an overall 0.70), I2 83%, 95% prediction interval -0.63 to 2.15. Subgroups: with cognitive factors 1.04 (0.54-1.53) versus without 0.37 (-0.22-0.95), Q(1)=2.91, p=0.09; session time Q(1)=1.41, p=0.24; frequency Q(2)=7.67, p=0.02, meta-regression b=0.264, p=0.001. Sleep (2 RCTs) SMD -2.07 (-6.76 to 2.62), not significant.
what_each_reports.P-699: Cai, Ma, Li, Lu, Geriatric Nursing 2023;51:351-359 (PROSPERO CRD42022347399). 10 RCTs of exergaming versus regular activities without exergaming (traditional physical activity, cognitive or physical-cognitive training, usual care) in adults >=60 with MCI (4 trials, n=166) or dementia (6 trials, n=350); 8 meta-analysed as mean differences on the original scales. MMSE pool (5 trials: Amjad 2019 in MCI; Padala 2012, Padala 2017, van Santen 2020, Zheng 2021 in dementia): MD 0.95, 95% CI -1.17 to 3.08, P=0.38, I2 74%; MD 2.49 (2.12-2.85) after excluding Padala 2012. MoCA pool (3 trials, all MCI: Amjad 2019, Liao 2020, Liu 2022): MD 2.12 (0.53-3.70), P=0.009, I2 98-99%; MD 1.35 (0.01-2.68) after excluding Amjad 2019. Abstract and conclusion report a cognitive benefit, with a caution for heterogeneity.

quantity_a: Pooled standardised mean difference (Hedges' g, random effects) in global cognition (MMSE, MoCA or NCSE) at end of intervention for single-modality aerobic exercise versus non-exercise controls (health education, stretching, usual activity), in RCTs of adults >=60 with MCI.
quantity_b: Pooled mean difference in MMSE points (random effects) at end of intervention for exergaming versus regular activities (mostly traditional physical activity, stretching or usual care), in 5 RCTs of adults >=60, four in dementia and one in MCI. P-699's MCI-only global-cognition estimate is a different pool (MoCA MD, 3 MCI trials).
incompatible_if_same: No. Both point estimates favour the intervention: SMD 0.76 (significant) against MMSE MD 0.95 (95% CI -1.17 to 3.08, non-significant). A difference in significance is not a data conflict (Section 5.2), and P-699's MCI-only pool shows a significant benefit (MoCA MD 2.12, 0.53-3.70), the same direction as P-698.

gates.task: match: T6 on both rows (intervention-efficacy syntheses).
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: the primary literatures pooled are disjoint; none of P-698's 11 aerobic-exercise RCTs is among P-699's 10 exergaming RCTs. No waiver on record.
gates.validation_tier: n/a (two evidence syntheses; counted as matched).
gates.modality_family: match at family level (exercise-class intervention measured with global-cognition screening scales), but the intervention differs within the family (aerobic exercise versus exergaming).

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: P-698 pools Hedges' g standardised differences across MMSE, MoCA and NCSE against non-exercise controls; P-699's contested pool is a raw MMSE mean difference against mostly active or usual-care controls in a majority-dementia set. Comparison, population and metric all differ; the registry's population-gate FAIL (MCI versus MCI, dementia) is correct.
independence: Independent: no shared primary trial. P-698 pools Bademli 2019, Chang 2021, Choi & Lee 2018, Doi 2017, Karthikeyan 2020, Law 2019, Song & Yu 2019, Tao 2019, Tsai 2019, Varela 2011 and Wei & Ji 2014; P-699 includes Liu 2022, Torpil 2021 (printed 'Torpi2021'), Zheng 2021, van Santen 2020, Amjad 2019, Karssemeijer 2019, Wiloth 2017, Padala 2017, Padala 2012 and Liao 2020. Different author teams (Korea; China); same journal volume only. This settles the trial-overlap check the record's residual_risk left open.
grounds: Both headline estimates favour the intervention (P-698 SMD 0.76, significant; P-699 MMSE MD 0.95, 95% CI -1.17 to 3.08, P = 0.38), so the claimed opposition is a significance-only difference, which Section 5.2 says is not a data conflict.

P-699's own headline is positive: its abstract reports a significant difference on MMSE and MoCA and its conclusion says exergaming improves cognition in older adults with MCI or dementia, so the reviews do not reach opposite verdicts.

P-699's null MMSE pool is four dementia trials plus one MCI trial, while its only MCI-only global-cognition pool (MoCA: Amjad 2019, Liao 2020, Liu 2022) shows a significant benefit (MD 2.12, 0.53-3.70), the same direction as P-698.
The record misreads P-699: the paper names no primary outcome, and the 'open problem' and 'abstract does not match the results table' sentences the record quotes are not in the PDF.

Were there a disagreement, the quantities would still differ: aerobic exercise against non-exercise controls on a standardised scale versus exergaming against mostly traditional physical activity or usual care on MMSE points, in MCI versus a mostly dementia pool, with the dataset-family gate unmatched.

record_defects: conflict_statement: the two reviews do not 'reach opposite headline verdicts'; P-699's abstract reports a significant difference on MMSE and MoCA and its conclusion states that exergaming improves cognition in older adults with MCI or dementia (with a caution for heterogeneity).
conflict_statement and claim_b call the MMSE pool P-699's 'PRIMARY' cognitive estimate; P-699 designates no primary outcome and reports the MMSE and MoCA pools side by side.

The record omits P-699's MCI-only MoCA pool (3 MCI trials, MD 2.12, 95% CI 0.53-3.70, P = 0.009), which agrees in direction with P-698; the null MMSE pool is four dementia trials plus one MCI trial (Amjad 2019).

claim_b ('pooling MCI AND dementia in one cognitive estimate (166 MCI across 4 trials, 350 dementia across 6 trials)'): those counts describe the 10 included trials; no single cognitive pool combines them (MMSE: 5 trials, 1 in MCI; MoCA: 3 trials, all MCI).

Quotes attributed to P-699 ('whether the cognitive benefits survive when MCI and dementia are analysed separately'; 'The most serious problem is that the abstract does not match the results table'; 'whether exergaming outperforms an equally dosed conventional physical-plus-cognitive training arm, which Liao 2020 specifically failed to show on MoCA') are not in the PDF; they are summary-block text (summaries.md lines 63217 and 63233). The abstract-versus-table mismatch they describe is real (the abstract lists MMSE, SPPB and PASE as significant; Table 2 gives P = 0.38, 0.87 and 0.11), and P-699 does report that Liao 2020 found no MoCA difference against physical-cognitive training.

claim_a ('its two dosing moderator claims rest on non-significant between-group tests'): the session-time contrast is non-significant (Q(1) = 1.41, p = 0.24), but the frequency moderator is significant (Q(2) = 7.67, p = 0.02; meta-regression b = 0.264, p = 0.001); the other non-significant contrast (cognitive factors, Q(1) = 2.91, p = 0.09) is about exercise type, not dose.

residual_risk ('P-699 never identifies which two of its ten trials were dropped'): not stated outright, but recoverable, since the pools list their references (MMSE 38, 42-44, 47; MoCA 38, 40, 41; SPPB/PASE 39, 44) and Torpil 2021 [45] and Wiloth 2017 [46] enter none; and the unchecked trial overlap it raises is now checked: the two reviews share no trial.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A disagreement would need an MCI-only exergaming (or aerobic-exercise) pool, with a comparable comparator and metric, whose interval excludes benefit or points the other way; P-699's MCI-only pool (MoCA) points the same way as P-698. Label alternative: documented_incommensurability (intervention, comparator, population and metric all differ; dataset family unmatched) if compatibility is judged only after the quantity question, as the operator did for C-234; no reading makes the pair genuine.
